data.name: Malkit
data.gender_notes: Malkit is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Malkit is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'mala' (garland) and 'kita' (fort). It is believed to be the name of the lord of the fort or the one who wears the garland of victory. The name Malkit carries the meaning “Lord of the fort” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Malkit usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the fort and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength and victory in life.
data.etymology: Malkit belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the fort.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Malkit total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Malkit holds a rich cultural significance in Hindu mythology as it is believed to be the name of various gods and goddesses. In Punjab, Malkit is particularly revered as the name of Baba Malook, a local deity worshipped for protection, prosperity, and forgiveness.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Malkit carries a deep spiritual significance as it symbolizes triumph, victory, and protection. It indicates the person named as one who is strong, powerful, and courageous, and is blessed with the Divine's favor. The 'mala' in the name signifies the garland of virtues and good qualities, and 'kita' symbolizes the fort of one's inner being, which is protected by the divine grace.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Malkit: Goddess of Fortune and Prosperity. Her name signifies the grace and power of the divine mother, bestowing wealth, abundance, and happiness upon her children.
